extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: NeedleBench is a comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual (English and Chinese) long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). It systematically embeds key data points at varying depths to test models' capabilities in diverse settings. Tasks are categorized into two scenarios: information-sparse (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) with minimal relevant details embedded within extensive irrelevant text, and information-dense (Ancestral Trace Challenge) where relevant information is continuously distributed throughout the context to simulate complex reasoning tasks.
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (Tsinghua University, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is largely synthetic, constructed programmatically. The 'needles' (key information units) are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts, deliberately designed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. The 'haystack' (background filler content) for English tasks is built using passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, from the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For English tasks, haystack content is from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset (Kamradt, 2023). For Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (Wei et al., 2023b) is used. Needles are synthetically generated fabricated facts and kinship statements.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the Ancestral Trace Challenge, relationship statements are randomly shuffled to eliminate positional bias. Names are randomly sampled from a name pool. Relationship terms are assigned with generation weights (1 for parent-child, 2 for grandparent-grandchild). For information-sparse tasks, needles are strategically inserted at various depths within the haystack.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer. To mitigate instruction truncation, a buffer is subtracted from the target context length when generating each input, ensuring models with different tokenizers are consistently exposed to the complete instructions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task were manually annotated, focusing on cases where the question type is 'identifying the eldest ancestor', to identify error categories including under-thinking, partial understanding errors, instruction following errors, repetitive output, hallucination errors, and other errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Error analysis identified main failure modes, with under-thinking being the most prevalent (60.2%), followed by partial understanding errors (12.9%), instruction following errors (7.5%), repetitive output (7.5%), hallucination errors (7.5%), and other errors (4.5%).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 tokenizer (tiktoken) for token length measurement; LMDeploy and vLLM for inference acceleration.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass. All reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset uses fictional synthetic names and relationships; no real personal or sensitive information is collected. Bilingual (English and Chinese) content is included.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Most evaluated models exhibit a performance gap between English and Chinese, with English scores typically higher, though some models (Qwen2.5-14B, GLM4-9B) perform slightly better in Chinese. These differences may be related to pretraining data distribution, tokenization strategies, or language-specific modeling approaches.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The authors note the need to expand it to cover more diverse and realistic information-dense scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation (benchmarking) of large language models' long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities, particularly for bilingual (English/Chinese) long-context tasks at adaptive context lengths. Used to assess retrieval at multiple depths, multi-needle retrieval, multi-needle reasoning, and information-dense ancestral trace reasoning.
